comment: Reference figures for AIA-0680, produced by calling torchvision's GeneralizedRCNNTransform rather than by re-implementing it. Regenerate with .venv-m3a/bin/python scripts/generate_torchvision_resize_oracle.py
toleranceReason: float32 sampling-coordinate granularity in torch's own kernel, amplified by the mod-256 discontinuities in the input pattern; measured worst 9.3e-5 on downscale2000x1500

cases.name: square512to800
cases.pins: The ticket's own figure: scale 1.5625, the non-integer factor no NN-spec resize mode can express. Square, so it says nothing about per-axis scales.

cases.name: nonSquare769x512
cases.pins: The two axes floor differently — 1201/769 against 800/512 — so an implementation carrying a single scalar scale fails here.

cases.name: nonSquare768x512
cases.pins: The trap. Non-square, but both axes scale by exactly 1.5625, so a single-scalar implementation PASSES. Present so the suite cannot mistake it for coverage.

cases.name: pageAspectRegion393x852
cases.pins: A third of a portrait phone snapshot, aspect 2.168. Above 1333/800 = 1.66625, so max_size binds and the short side never reaches min_size — the case the 'scales the short side to min_size' shorthand gets wrong.

cases.name: downscale2000x1500
cases.pins: Scale below 1. A half-pixel rule implemented for upsampling only breaks here, and it is the one case where the two align_corners conventions also disagree at the low corner, because there the false-convention coordinate is positive and unclamped.

cases.name: knifeEdge646x1077
cases.pins: The floor knife-edge. max_size binds, yet 1077 · (1333/1077) evaluates just below 1333 in float64, so the long side lands on 1332 and the short on 799 — one pixel short on BOTH axes. An implementation that assumes the binding side reaches its limit exactly, or that evaluates the product in a different precision or order, disagrees here and nowhere else in this list.

cases.name: boundaryAspect800x1333
cases.pins: Sits exactly on the 1333/800 = 1.66625 aspect boundary where the binding rule changes hands, and both candidate scales come out at exactly 1.0 — so the resize is an identity and only the padding acts. Pins the degenerate branch and the pad value together. It is deliberately NOT named for a tie-break: the two scales being equal at 1.0 exercises no tie-break at all, since min() returns the same number either way. A scan of long sides 801…6000 for two candidate scales within 1e-12 of each other that straddle a floor boundary found only exact-ratio coincidences (1333x800, 2666x1600, 3999x2400, 5332x3200), all of which land on integers; no non-trivial contested tie exists in that range.

cases.name: degenerate1x1
cases.pins: The smallest input the trust boundary can be handed. Exercises the low-side clamp, where the align_corners=False source coordinate 0.5·a − 0.5 is negative and has to be pinned to source pixel 0 rather than read out of bounds.
